cards.explanation: The answer is cherubim, skillfully worked right into the linen. God says it again for the veil, "…with cherubim skillfully worked into it." (Exodus 26:31). Those curtains and that veil were works of art, and I'm over here proud when my stamp comes out straight.

The answer is so the tabernacle is one unit. That's the reason God gives. The fifty gold clasps join the two sets of curtains "…so that the tabernacle will be a unit." Two sets of five go in, and one tabernacle comes out, which is the kind of teamwork I like to see.

The answer is False. Nothing gets trimmed. The half curtain left over "…shall hang down over the back of the tabernacle." And the tent curtains will be a cubit longer on either side, with the excess hanging over the sides to cover it (Exodus 26:12-13). The extra is part of the plan, and I wish my cookie crumbs were treated that well.

The word is pattern. God says to set up the tabernacle "…according to the pattern shown you on the mountain." Moses isn't making it up as he goes. He was shown it, and that's more than I get with half my recipes.

The answer is the ark of the Testimony. God says to "…place the ark of the Testimony behind the veil." The veil then separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place (Exodus 26:33). The ark gets the room behind the veil, and the mercy seat goes on top of it (Exodus 26:34).

The room behind the veil is the Most Holy Place. God says the veil "…will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place." (Exodus 26:33). The ark sits back there, and the mercy seat goes on top of it (Exodus 26:34). The name tells you something, friends.

The answer is True. God says, "Put the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place." (Exodus 26:34). The ark sits behind the veil, and the mercy seat goes right on top of it. That's a good, clear instruction.

The answer is outside the veil, across from each other. God says to place the table outside the veil on the north side, and the lampstand opposite it on the south side (Exodus 26:35). Both stay outside the veil, facing each other across the room. I'd call that a very organized room.

The answer is False. The posts are overlaid with gold and use gold hooks, but God says to "…cast five bronze bases for them." (Exodus 26:37). The wall frames stand on silver bases (Exodus 26:19). Same tent, different metal at the bottom.

The answer is horn, one on each of the four corners. God says to make them "…so that the horns are of one piece…" so they're part of the altar and not stuck on afterward. The whole altar then gets overlaid with bronze.

The answer is bronze, friends! The altar is overlaid with bronze, and the instruction says, "Make all its utensils of bronze…" (Exodus 27:3). Then the grate is bronze mesh with bronze rings (Exodus 27:4), the poles are overlaid with bronze (Exodus 27:6), and even the tent pegs are bronze (Exodus 27:19). Pots, shovels, bowls, forks, firepans, all one metal, a perfectly matching set. My spoons have never matched once, and I've stopped asking why.

The answer is so the altar can be carried. The poles "…are to be inserted into the rings so that the poles are on two sides of the altar when it is carried." Slide the poles in and it's ready to travel. I could use poles like that for my cookie trays.

The answer is False. God says, "Construct the altar with boards so that it is hollow." He adds that it is "…to be made just as you were shown on the mountain." Hollow it is, and I bet it carries easier too.

The answer is the courtyard gate. The east side is fifty cubits wide, with fifteen cubits of curtain on each end. In between, "The gate of the courtyard shall be twenty cubits long…" (Exodus 27:14-16). Fifteen and fifteen and twenty makes fifty, so the math works out.

The answer is False. God says the gate has "…a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen." (Exodus 27:16). It's the same blue, purple and scarlet the tabernacle curtains have. That gate shows up in color.

The answer is all the time, friends. The oil of pressed olives is for the light, and the lamps are to keep burning continually (Exodus 27:20). Then Aaron and his sons are to tend them "…from evening until morning." (Exodus 27:21). Evening until morning! I fall asleep waiting for one batch to cool, so I'd be the worst lamp crew in the camp.
The answer is Aaron and his sons. God says, "…Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps before the LORD…" (Exodus 27:21). Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). So the lamp job stays in the family.

The answer is True! Aaron and his sons are to tend the lamps "…from evening until morning." They do it in the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil, before the LORD (Exodus 27:21). That's the whole night shift, and I wouldn't trade my days for it.

The answer is False, friends. Tending the lamps isn't just for the wilderness. God says, "This is to be a permanent statute for the Israelites for the generations to come." (Exodus 27:21). Permanent, plus generations to come, means this one is meant to last.
